details:
Project Overview

Concordia is an interactive concept study for a future human settlement on Mars, located in the Utopia Planitia region. It combines settlement planning, engineering data, architectural visualization, systems thinking, and immersive storytelling to explore how a large-scale Mars base could function as a connected and livable environment.

The project works as a browser-based 3D walkthrough. Users can explore the proposed settlement from a human-scale, first-person perspective or switch to an overview mode. They can move between major structures using fast travel, inspect buildings and infrastructure, view supplied blueprint sheets, activate cutaway and interior modes, and follow a cinematic journey from Earth to Mars. The project also includes an evidence “Ledger” containing calculations, live calculators, limitations, open questions, model references, and provenance labels distinguishing referenced information, assumptions, generated content, and pending items.

Benefits

Concordia makes a complex settlement proposal easier to understand than a conventional technical document or static site. It allows users to see how habitats, farms, energy systems, transport routes, medical areas, industrial zones, communications, radiation protection, reactors, gravity wheels, and other infrastructure relate spatially.

The project also supports more transparent design review. Instead of presenting every value as certain, it identifies assumptions, approximations, missing drawings, unresolved questions, and areas requiring further engineering validation. This helps engineers, architects, researchers, educators, and the public discuss the project using a shared visual and technical reference.

Intended Impact

The intended impact is to improve how early-stage Mars settlement concepts are communicated, evaluated, and developed. Concordia encourages people to think of a Mars base as an interconnected community and infrastructure system rather than a collection of isolated buildings.

It is designed to support interdisciplinary collaboration, help identify dependencies and risks, make technical information more accessible, and encourage better questions about human life on Mars. The project does not claim to be final construction documentation or validated engineering sign-off. Its purpose is to create a credible, structured foundation for further research, testing, and design development.

Tools and Technologies

The project was developed as a client-side web application using:

  • TypeScript for application logic and data handling
  • Three.js for the interactive 3D settlement environment
  • Vite for development and production builds
  • HTML and CSS for the interface and visual system
  • JSON for structured settlement data, calculations, journey stages, and metadata
  • SVG for engineering blueprint sheets and technical drawings
  • Canvas rendering for the small animated robot guide
  • Git and npm for project management and dependency handling

The project runs in a modern web browser and does not require specialized hardware. A desktop computer with a mouse and keyboard provides the best experience, while lightweight touch controls support smaller screens and mobile devices. No physical hardware was required beyond standard development computers.

Creativity

Concordia is creative because it combines technical communication with interactive spatial storytelling. Rather than showing the proposal through only diagrams, text, or slides, it lets users inhabit the settlement, experience its distances, inspect its structures, and move between different levels of information.

The visual design combines a Mars-inspired landscape with an instrumented mission-console interface. Technical elements such as provenance tags, blueprint viewers, coordinate readouts, cutaway views, and live calculations are integrated into the exploration experience. The project also uses a cinematic journey and an animated robot guide to make a highly technical subject more accessible and emotionally engaging.

Factors Considered

The team considered technical accuracy, transparency, human scale, usability, performance, accessibility, and visual communication. Supplied data and drawings were preserved as the primary reference material, while approximated terrain, representative interiors, and illustrative journey content were clearly identified.

The design also considered Mars-specific conditions, including low gravity, limited atmosphere, radiation exposure, dust storms, long travel distances, energy needs, agriculture, resource extraction, transportation, emergency access, and psychological wellbeing. From a user-experience perspective, the team considered intuitive navigation, responsive layouts, readable data, mobile limitations, clear warnings, and the need to distinguish evidence from assumptions.

Ultimately, Concordia was designed to balance scientific ambition with intellectual honesty: it imagines what a future Mars settlement could become while clearly communicating what is known, what is assumed, and what still needs to be solved.
